task.question: A coherently controlled SELECT applies, for each selector value s, a permutation p_s of the system register, while leaving the coefficient and selector registers fixed. Prove that the map sending (coeff, (s, x)) to (coeff, (s, p_s(x))) is a genuine bijection of the whole product register by exhibiting its two-sided inverse, and explain why its matrix is automatically unitary. Why is it essential that the inverse applies the inverse permutation (p_s)^{-1} indexed by the SAME selector value s that is read on input?

by
  intro ι fi di first second
  have collapse : ∀ (operator : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (row column : ι),
      (∑ k : ι, QuantumBlockEncoding.Robin.ComplexLCU.equivPermutationMatrix second row k * operator k column) =
        operator (second.symm row) column :=
    by
      intro operator row column
      classical
      rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (second.symm row)]
      · simp [QuantumBlockEncoding.Robin.ComplexLCU.equivPermutationMatrix]
      · intro candidate _ candidate_ne
        have miss : row ≠ second candidate := by
          intro hit
          apply candidate_ne
          apply second.injective
          calc
            second candidate = row := hit.symm
            _ = second (second.symm row) := (second.apply_symm_apply row).symm
        simp [QuantumBlockEncoding.Robin.ComplexLCU.equivPermutationMatrix, miss]
      · simp
  have composition : QuantumBlockEncoding.Robin.ComplexLCU.equivPermutationMatrix second * QuantumBlockEncoding.Robin.ComplexLCU.equivPermutationMatrix first =
      QuantumBlockEncoding.Robin.ComplexLCU.equivPermutationMatrix (first.trans second) := by
    ext row column
    rw [Matrix.mul_apply, collapse]
    simp only [QuantumBlockEncoding.Robin.ComplexLCU.equivPermutationMatrix, Equiv.trans_apply]
    by_cases hit : second.symm row = first column
    · have forward : row = second (first column) := by
        rw [← hit]
        exact (second.apply_symm_apply row).symm
      simp [hit, forward]
    · have miss : row ≠ second (first column) := by
        intro forward
        apply hit
        rw [forward, second.symm_apply_apply]
      simp [hit, miss]
  refine ⟨collapse, composition, ?_⟩
  intro state
  rw [← composition]
  exact (Matrix.mulVec_mulVec state (QuantumBlockEncoding.Robin.ComplexLCU.equivPermutationMatrix second)
    (QuantumBlockEncoding.Robin.ComplexLCU.equivPermutationMatrix first)).symm

task.question: Finite basis permutations are represented by 0/1 matrices: for a bijection e of the index set, its matrix has a 1 at (row, column) exactly when row = e(column). Prove that composing two such permutation matrices multiplies them in reverse order: the matrix of the composite that does 'first then second' equals (matrix of second) times (matrix of first). Make explicit how matrix multiplication selects a single surviving term and why the order reversal is forced rather than a convention.

by
  have qcb_step_jet104_jet_iff : ∀ (p q : Polynomial ℝ) (a : ℝ) (k : ℕ), (∀ j ≤ k, (Polynomial.derivative^[j] p).eval a = (Polynomial.derivative^[j] q).eval a) ↔ (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) ^ (k + 1) ∣ p - q :=
    by
      intro p q a k
      constructor
      · intro h
        have ht : Polynomial.X ^ (k + 1) ∣ Polynomial.taylor a (p - q) := by
          apply Polynomial.X_pow_dvd_iff.mpr
          intro j hj
          have he : (j.factorial : ℝ) * (Polynomial.taylor a (p - q)).coeff j = 0 := by
            rw [← QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.eval_iterate_derivative]
            simp only [Polynomial.iterate_derivative_sub, Polynomial.eval_sub,
              h j (by omega), sub_self]
          exact (mul_eq_zero.mp he).resolve_left (by exact_mod_cast Nat.factorial_ne_zero j)
        have hm := map_dvd (Polynomial.taylorAlgHom (-a)) ht
        simpa [Polynomial.taylor_taylor, ← sub_eq_add_neg] using hm
      · intro h j hj
        exact QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.jet_eq_of_pow_dvd_sub p q a k j hj h
  have qcb_step_jet104_left : ∀ (k : ℕ) (p q : Polynomial ℝ), (∀ j ≤ k, (Polynomial.derivative^[j] p).eval (-1) = (Polynomial.derivative^[j] q).eval (-1)) → QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.leftModulus k ∣ p - q :=
    by
      intro k p q h
      exact (qcb_step_jet104_jet_iff p q (-1) k).mp h
  have qcb_step_jet104_right : ∀ (k : ℕ) (p q : Polynomial ℝ), (∀ j ≤ k, (Polynomial.derivative^[j] p).eval 0 = (Polynomial.derivative^[j] q).eval 0) → QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.rightModulus k ∣ p - q :=
    by
      intro k p q h
      exact (qcb_step_jet104_jet_iff p q 0 k).mp h
  have qcb_step_jet104_coprime : ∀ (k : ℕ), IsCoprime (QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.leftModulus k) (QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.rightModulus k) :=
    by
      intro k
      unfold QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.leftModulus
        QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.rightModulus
      apply IsCoprime.pow
      exact Polynomial.isCoprime_X_sub_C_of_isUnit_sub (by norm_num)
  have qcb_step_jet104_product : ∀ (k : ℕ) (p q : Polynomial ℝ), (∀ j ≤ k, (Polynomial.derivative^[j] p).eval (-1) = (Polynomial.derivative^[j] q).eval (-1)) → (∀ j ≤ k, (Polynomial.derivative^[j] p).eval 0 = (Polynomial.derivative^[j] q).eval 0) → (QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.leftModulus k) * (QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.rightModulus k) ∣ p - q :=
    by
      intro k p q hl hr
      exact (qcb_step_jet104_coprime k).mul_dvd
        (qcb_step_jet104_left k p q hl) (qcb_step_jet104_right k p q hr)
  have qcb_step_jet104_degree : ∀ (k : ℕ), ((QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.leftModulus k) * (QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.rightModulus k)).natDegree = 2 * k + 2 :=
    by
      intro k
      unfold QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.leftModulus
        QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.rightModulus
      rw [Polynomial.natDegree_mul (pow_ne_zero _ (Polynomial.X_sub_C_ne_zero _))
        (pow_ne_zero _ (Polynomial.X_sub_C_ne_zero _))]
      simp only [Polynomial.natDegree_pow, Polynomial.natDegree_X_sub_C, mul_one]
      omega
  have qcb_step_jet104_annihilate : ∀ (k : ℕ) (d : Polynomial ℝ), d.natDegree ≤ 2 * k + 1 → (QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.leftModulus k) * (QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.rightModulus k) ∣ d → d = 0 :=
    by
      intro k d hb hdiv
      by_contra hne
      have hd := Polynomial.natDegree_le_of_dvd hdiv hne
      rw [qcb_step_jet104_degree k] at hd
      omega
  intro k p q hp hq hl hr
  apply sub_eq_zero.mp
  exact qcb_step_jet104_annihilate k (p - q)
    ((Polynomial.natDegree_sub_le p q).trans (max_le hp hq))
    (qcb_step_jet104_product k p q hl hr)

task.question: Fix a real point a and a natural number k, and prescribe target values v(0), v(1), ..., v(k). Define a degree-at-most-k real polynomial P by taking the local Taylor polynomial centred at a whose coefficient of (x-a)^j is v(j)/j!. Prove that for every j with 0 <= j <= k the ordinary j-th derivative of P evaluated at a equals exactly v(j). You may use the fact that the j-th derivative of a polynomial at a point equals j! times the degree-j Taylor coefficient of the polynomial about that point.
